review_method: Fresh independent reading of the complete packet and applicable global, repository, editorial, source, document-schema and three-document/liturgical profile guidance.

Read the complete canonical study: main.tex and all seven authored section files, together with the publication/element manifests, verified appointed-text record, scope, interpretation account, source bindings and declared review dependencies. Revisited the two developed readings and terminal qualifications after checking their sources.

Read exact retained source texts and viewed the identified original page images independently. Previous context/research reviewer result files and review conclusions were not used as evidence. Read source-receipts.json for identities and delivery locations, and inspected current exact artifact records for relevant sources.

Recomputed the 19 engine-sealed input hashes before and after inspection. Independently rehashed all 18 retained acquired deliveries, 29 retained text witnesses, the offline archive and its nine members. The text and member records also match their actual bytes. These integrity checks are not claims to whole-work reading, fresh acquisition, or corpus-wide validation.
Did not delegate, edit reviewed artifacts, commit, push, run a workflow transition, or write outside the assigned scratch directory.

mode_and_scope.outcome: The publication manifest, reviewed scope/verified text and production-plan authorization agree on complete appointed text. No reference-only exception is invoked. The conditional Research PDF locator/anchor checks therefore do not apply.
mode_and_scope.inventory: Eleven appointed elements are present: composite Introit with its separate psalm verse, Collect, Epistle, Gradual, Alleluia, Gospel, Offertory, Secret, Trinity Preface, Communion, Postcommunion. Ordinary cues and historical short conclusions are preserved and explained.
mode_and_scope.occurrence: The universal-calendar resumed Sixth Sunday identity and exclusions are consistent with RG18(b), precedence, RG109/111(b) and RGMR298. The retained November 2026 ICRSP entry explicitly names the twenty-fifth Sunday after Pentecost/sixth after Epiphany, Gloria, Creed and Trinity Preface; its Oratio pro Papa remains an institutional addition. The retained FSSPX delivery identifies VI Sunday after Epiphany (Transferred) for 2026-11-15. This is inspection of the dated retained deliveries, not a fresh live-site claim.
mode_and_scope.optional_print: No print PDF was assigned or reviewed. No 20–50-page certification, pagination, layout, export or live-link certification is supplied.
mode_and_scope.chronology: The generated Scriptural Date and Location appendix was not re-reviewed as authored prose or re-adjudicated for dates, as the packet requires. No authored sentence elsewhere was found to replace its disputed chronology with a newly asserted event/composition date.

interpretation_assessment.reading_A: The word received in trial becomes a witness to others. Chrysostom supplies the sequence-specific missionary problem, contact through leaven and virtue/miracles distinction; Aquinas supplies active faith, charity, hope, qualified imitation, preaching alternatives and final expectation. These are substantive contributions from distinct eligible authors. Augustine, Jerome and Bede develop related questions without replacing the main reasoning.
interpretation_assessment.reading_B: The Gospel reforms the whole person and teaches desire. Jerome supplies scriptural knowledge and ordered faculties; Augustine supplies love as leaven, the cry acknowledging need, propitiation and resurrection-directed hope. Bellarmine adds a distinct account of penitence and Bede constrains confident prayer through charity. This is substantively different from repeating Reading A’s public witness theme.
interpretation_assessment.four_senses: Each reading has its own four-senses conclusion grounded in its developed argument. Literal sense concerns the actual narrative/epistle/prayer actions; allegorical sense concerns Christ and the Church; moral sense concerns transformed conduct; anagogical sense concerns resurrection and final deliverance. Moral application does not substitute for literal setting or final hope.
interpretation_assessment.comparison: The final comparison preserves actual differences over the three measures, characterizes the readings as complementary, and does not invent doctrinal disagreement or historical compositional intent.
interpretation_assessment.depth: Both readings explain particular questions and the source’s inference at length, then reason through liturgical consequences. Every element contributes in the running exposition. Neither reading begins or closes with a coverage roll call. No gallery, generic theme list or four-senses table supplies missing development.
